articles.summary: Key Takeaways Thin hair refers to hair density, not strand thickness. You can have fine, medium, or coarse strands and still have thin hair if fewer follicles are present on the scalp. Thin hair and thinning hair are not the same. Thin hair is typically determined by genetics, while thinning hair often involves increased shedding or hair loss. Volume starts with understanding your hair's structure. Hair density, strand diameter, scalp health, and styling habits all influence how full hair appears. Heavy products can weigh thin hair down. Lightweight conditioners, leave-ins, and styling products help support volume without creating buildup. The right routine can help thin hair look fuller. Volumizing products, strategic styling techniques, and personalized hair care can enhance body and movement.
articles.title: Thin Hair vs. Thinning Hair: What's the Difference and How to Care for Thin Hair
